Subject: Prompt output storage & lifecycle — follow-up from today's call

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the specific items you asked us to confirm on PII and prompt/output handling: 

1) What Redwood stores from prompts/outputs by default (hosted API):
- Request logs: request metadata (timestamp, model, route) retained for 90 days.
- Prompt text & generated output: by default Redwood Hosted stores prompt + output for 30 days to power troubleshooting, quality monitoring, and to support customer support tickets.
- KV/prefix caches: in-memory ephemeral (not written to long-term object storage) and are evicted per policy.

2) Training/Model updates: Redwood does not use hosted customer prompts/outputs to train public model weights. Customers can opt-in to telemetry for product improvement separately.

3) Data residency: Hosted logs and artifacts are stored in the region you select (us-west/us-east/eu). For Helix, we confirmed US-only storage for the POC.

4) Private deployments: if you run Redwood Private (VPC), storage retention is under your control and can be set to zero (no prompt/output persistence) or configured to your long-term retention policy.

Next steps I promised on the call:
- Send a short one-pager summarizing the points above + SOC2 summary link (attached).
- Karthik will reply with the technical placement of caches and how long short-lived debugging artifacts persist.
- Marissa will outline the contractual language we typically add around data use and non-training commitments.

If any of the bullets above are inconsistent with what you heard, please flag and we'll adjust. Ready to jump on another call with security if you'd like a deeper technical walkthrough.

Cheers,

Hi Alice — quick technical clarifications per your questions: 

- Configurability: For Hosted customers, retention of prompt + output is configurable per account via the Console. Options: 
  * 0 days (transient-only): prompts/outputs not written to persistent object storage; short-lived debug artifacts may still be created in ephemeral stores and are auto-deleted within 24 hours.
  * 7 days, 30 days, 90 days (preset tiers) — longer terms available with contractual agreement.

- Backups & cross-region: We do not replicate persistent prompt/output blobs across regions by default. Snapshots for platform state (not including prompt payloads) are region-scoped. If you require strict single-region guarantees we can enable region-scoped policies and document them in the contract.

- Logs that contain full prompt text: Request bodies that contain prompt text are considered prompt data. Those are subject to the same retention policy you choose. Access to raw prompt text in logs is restricted to a small set of authorized SRE/infra roles and is audited.

- Private deployment option: With Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) you control the object stores and retention; our installer has an option to disable persistent prompt/output altogether.

I'll attach a short infra sketch and a SOC2 pointer in the follow-up note (attached to Jonas' message). Happy to do a security deep-dive; propose Tue if that works.

Alice — looping in legal/CS language you can expect in the MSA for clarity: 

- Data usage: Redwood will not use customer prompts/outputs from Hosted accounts to train or improve models used by other customers. This will be spelled out in the Data Use section.
- Retention SLA: For Hosted accounts we will commit to the retention tier selected in the Console and to delete prompt/output artifacts per that schedule unless otherwise required by subpoena or legal hold.
- Region controls: Contract will specify the chosen region of storage; Redwood will not replicate prompt/output artifacts outside the agreed region unless Helix authorizes it in writing.
- Audit: We can provide periodic audit extracts for the POC (redacted as appropriate) and SOC2 report access via our compliance portal link.

If you'd like, I can draft the short contract addendum that codifies the 0-day/30-day options and the non-training promise and share it with your procurement folks. Jonas — can you propose a Tue/Wed security walkthrough slot?
